title: Does an atlas pack its parts' indexes into one file, as an archive does?
body:
sail-9d931d decided that an atlas points at per-file `.saidx` files: `libsail::atlas::Atlas` writes a `.satlas` holding each part's path, stamp and record count, and each part keeps its own `.saidx` beside it. This reopens that choice with a layout the original options did not consider: one file holding every part's `.saidx` the way an archive holds its members.

tar stores each member as a 512-byte header and the member's bytes, with no table of contents, so finding a member means walking every header before it. zip adds a central directory at the end of the file and a fixed-size footer pointing at it. A reader seeks to any member from the directory, and a rewritten member is appended along with a new directory, leaving the old copy as dead bytes.

## Options

1. By reference, as built. N + 1 files on disk. A sample opens the atlas and each part's `.saidx` it touches. Editing one part rewrites that part's `.saidx`. Every part stays usable on its own.
2. Packed, zip-style. One file holding every part's `.saidx` byte for byte, each padded to 8 bytes, followed by a table and a fixed footer:

```text
SLAT header: version, format
part 0's .saidx, byte-identical, padded to 8
part 1's .saidx, byte-identical, padded to 8
...
table: per part, path, stamp, count, and the part's start and end here
footer: where the table starts
```

3. Both. By reference stays the default, and `sail atlas --pack` writes the packed form for an atlas that will not change. The table says per part whether its index is inline or at a path.

| concern | by reference | packed |
|---|---|---|
| files on disk | N + 1 | 1 |
| opens for a sample | 1 + parts touched | 1 |
| offsets of every part | one mapping per part | one mapping, zero-copy once sail-bb932e aligns `.saidx` |
| editing one part | rewrite its `.saidx` | append the part and a new table, the old copy is dead bytes |
| dead bytes | none | grow until a compaction pass |
| a part used alone | as is | after extracting its region, one copy |
| code | done | a base offset in `Index::open`, the table, the footer, compaction |

At the target scale the offsets alone are about 19.6 GB, which is why rewriting inline offsets in place lost the first time. Packing avoids an in-place rewrite by appending, at the cost of dead bytes.

## Open

What decides this is a measurement no one has taken: time spent opening per-part `.saidx` files against time spent reading records, for a sample drawn from an atlas of about a thousand parts, on the `benchmarks/` setup. If the opens are a small share, option 1 stays. If they dominate, option 2 or 3 is worth its code.

No lean until that number exists.
